claim: Calling IsValid() inside CommandResponseFromJSON makes the previously lenient parser an all-or-nothing gate on two live integration ingress paths (app/command.go:595 outgoing slash commands and web/webhook.go:114 command webhooks): a payload with a valid parent and one bad extra_responses entry (or an over-long Text) used to deliver the parent post but now fails the whole parse and posts nothing, converting partial delivery into total failure with no config flag, deprecation window, or changelog.
raw: #1 🟠 High: Parse-time rejection discards responses that previously delivered posts, breaking existing integrations

claim: CommandResponseFromHTTPBody only routes application/json bodies through CommandResponseFromJSON; a text/plain body goes to CommandResponseFromPlainText which never validates, so an integration bypasses the new Text length limit (and validation entirely) by flipping the Content-Type header — a 100000-byte text/plain body parses with no error.
raw: #4 🟡 Medium: The length limit is bypassed entirely by sending `Content-Type: text/plain`

raw: #5 🟡 Medium: The Go client now rejects valid 200 responses from the server, including plugin-produced ones

claim: The recursive IsValid call over ExtraResponses returns the child's *AppError verbatim with the same Where, Id and DetailedError, so a nested extra_responses validation failure is byte-identical to a top-level one and carries no index, path or nesting marker for the integration author debugging the rejection.
raw: #6 🟢 Low: A nested `extra_responses` failure is indistinguishable from a top-level one

raw: #7 🟢 Low: The new length test cannot distinguish bytes from runes, leaving the ambiguity in #3 unguarded
